text:
maya: Pushed the prefetch-scheduler + kernel-handoff tweak to canary this morning. Quick summary: p50 -10%, p95 -20%, projected infra token cost -27% for convo-heavy tenants.

ev an: Nice. What's "kernel-handoff" in this change?

maya: It's a tiny heuristic in the scheduler that prefers quantized kernels for <256 seq and hands off long sequences to float kernels earlier to avoid wasted compute. Works with the prefetch scheduler that staggers KV reads to avoid spikes.

ev an: Canary numbers?

deploy-bot: Canary report (prefetch-sched-2026-08-01): 80k requests, median seq 44, p50 46ms -> 41ms, p95 230ms -> 184ms, error rate stable 0.02% -> 0.02%. Dash: https://internal.redwood/perf/prefetch-sched-2026-08-01

sam: Any host regressions?

maya: Small coordinator CPU increase (~5%) under very bursty traffic; added a backoff that disables prefetch when mem usage >82% or when host CPU >78%. No customer regressions seen.

ev an: Rollout plan?

maya: Canary -> 4% -> 30% (6h) -> 100% (36h). Auto-rollback if p95 rises >4% or error rate delta >0.12%. Alerts added to runbook.

cost-bot: If fleet-wide, projected monthly token infra spend reduction ~25-30%. Logged under COST-2026-08-PREFETCH.

sre-bot: Added perf thresholds to eng-sre runbook and created an incident playbook note for cache-churn scenarios.

maya: I'll post the config snippet and a short how-it-works note in #docs shortly and draft a 1-slide summary for all-hands.

ev an: Nice work! Can we follow up with a small experiment to learn if a learned predictor beats the heuristic?

maya: Yep adding that spike to the backlog.
